scope: Hermux right-panel responsiveness LOGIC across 5 files: ordered forwarder (FIFO+coalescing), bounded drain loop, adaptive preview refresh, scrollback fast/slow split, paste chunking
hinge_logic: The single ordered keystroke forwarder (forwarder.rs spawn_forwarder + main.rs:578 wiring + drain loop at main.rs:660-1184). It is the load-bearing path for the user's #1 complaint (typing latency). Verdict: architecturally sound — FIFO order is guaranteed by single-sender + order-preserving mpsc + single sequential consumer; coalescing is correct (same-session only, flush-before-Key). The one logic smell on this hinge is space-routed-as-Key defeating text coalescing for prose (F2).

user_need_match.quote: la réactivité quand je tape du texte dans le panel Hermux (droite) est très lente; le scroll souris/pad marche mal; le copier-coller de long texte bug. Rends-le 100% instant + corrige scroll + paste, en gardant toutes les options.
user_need_match.evidence: All three complaints are logically addressed by the committed responsiveness work. TYPING LAG: the per-keystroke blocking rmux RPC (5-15ms) was removed by the process-wide pane_cache (session.rs:117,266 pane_for) + connect_cached singleton (session.rs:143) + off-loop ordered forwarder (main.rs:578, forwarder.rs) so the event loop only does a non-blocking channel send (main.rs:1050). SCROLL: position-aware mouse scroll (input.rs:111 scroll_active_panel_at, column>=30 → preview) plus the follow_tail/preview_scroll model (app.rs:860-888) and the scrollback heavy-path (app.rs:1021 capture_pane_history) give real history to scroll into. PASTE: long paste is forwarded as ONE bracketed-paste block with body chunked at 4096-byte char boundaries and NO auto-Enter (session.rs:497 send_paste_raw, forwarder.rs Paste variant) so embedded newlines no longer submit each line. Score 82 (not 100) reflects optimization HEADROOM (F2-F6), not a broken feature.
edge_cases_covered: fast typing FIFO order (single consumer, falsified)
multi-line paste no per-line submit (bracketed paste markers)
very large paste chunked on UTF-8 char boundaries (session.rs:511-514)
scroll re-glues to live tail at offset 0 (app.rs:864)
stale pane after kill+recreate self-heals on hot send/capture paths (is_pane_stale retry)

falsifiable_tests.actual: single sender = the single-threaded event loop (sends in keystroke order); tokio unbounded mpsc preserves send order; ONE consumer task awaits each send sequentially before the next. falsifiable_tests.name: bounded drain cannot starve redraw

Bounded by min(queue-empty, 8ms) every tick. Redraw/preview/housekeeping below always runs.

issues_found_and_fixed.issue: Dead function `shell_escape` — zero call sites (team.rs has its own used copy); compiler dead_code warning
issues_found_and_fixed.fix_applied: Removed the 3-line dead function. Build re-verified: warning gone, 0 errors.

issues_documented_not_fixed.issue: Routing the space char as a named Key 'Space' flushes the forwarder's pending coalesced text, defeating Text coalescing for ANY multi-word input — a prose sentence becomes ~1 send_text per word instead of 1 per burst. This is on the user's PRIME hot path (typing prose). The justifying comment ('a bare " " literal sometimes renders as the word space') is almost certainly a misdiagnosis: send_text_raw forwards literal UTF-8 bytes, and every other printable char is trusted to that same path; a 0x20 byte cannot echo as the string 'space' unless the SDK key-name-translates whitespace (it does not).
issues_documented_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: First Law: changing space→Text without a live-session echo test risks reintroducing a VISIBLE regression (spaces rendering as 'space') if the comment's premise is somehow correct. The asymmetry (visible on-screen regression vs minor RPC overhead) makes a blind change unsafe. RECOMMENDED FIX (verify-first): on a live rmux session, send_text(" ") and confirm the pane echoes a space; if so, route space through ForwardMsg::Text to restore coalescing on the prose path.

issues_documented_not_fixed.issue: While browsing history (follow_tail==false) the preview re-spawns the `rmux` CLI subprocess (~12 times/sec at 80ms idle cadence) and re-fetches the SAME 1000 scrollback lines each tick. Fork+exec per refresh is heavy vs the SDK snapshot used on the tail path.
issues_documented_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: Bounded and only during active history browsing — NOT the typing hot path the user complained about. Caching history-on-enter adds state + staleness risk while the agent keeps producing output above the fold; SIMPLICITY-COMPLETE + surgical-changes discipline says do not add that complexity speculatively. Documented as future optimization if history-scroll lag is ever reported. Root cause is an SDK gap (no scrollback API), not a logic defect.

issues_documented_not_fixed.issue: Unlike its siblings (send_text_raw / send_key / capture_pane), send_paste_raw has NO is_pane_stale invalidate+retry. A kill+recreate of the session mid-paste (after the \e[200~ opener, before \e[201~ closer) would leave the target app stuck in bracketed-paste mode.
issues_documented_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: Very low probability (requires session kill+recreate during the few ms of a paste). A correct retry is non-trivial (must not resend a half-delivered block). Documented; not worth the added branching complexity for a rare path.

issues_documented_not_fixed.issue: refresh_preview() is invoked from three sites per loop (adaptive cadence, on selection/tab change inside the drain, and the 2s fallback). On a tick where selection changed AND the cadence elapsed, two captures fire in the same tick.
issues_documented_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: Each trigger serves a distinct purpose (instant feedback on nav vs steady cadence vs liveness fallback); the rare double-capture is one extra cheap snapshot. Consolidating would couple the triggers and reduce nav responsiveness. Negligible.

issues_documented_not_fixed.issue: Cold action handlers (kill/create/open/planner) call SessionManager::connect() — a fresh rmux daemon socket (~30-50ms) — while connect_cached() exists and is used on hot paths.
issues_documented_not_fixed.why_not_fixed: These are user-initiated one-shot actions, not hot paths; the 30-50ms is imperceptible against the action's own latency. Consistency-only nit; out of the responsiveness budget.

confidence_basis: high. Every applied change and core claim was verified by a run command, not by reading: cargo build run pre+post fix (Finished, 0 errors); the shell_escape removal proven safe by zero grep call-sites AND the compiler's dead_code warning disappearing post-fix; clippy run across the workspace showing no hot-path lint; FIFO/coalescing/drain-bound claims falsified by explicit logic traces with no surviving reorder/starvation path. The ONE thing I could not verify on live runtime is the space-as-Key premise (no live rmux echo test was run) — and precisely because of that I did NOT apply a change there (First Law), so it cannot lower confidence in what was shipped. Score 82/B+ is an honest quality grade with documented optimization headroom; the user's three responsiveness complaints are all logically addressed by the committed architecture.
